sections.h2: Choosing a sale route in Henrietta
sections.html:
Repairs and timing should drive your choice. Around Rochester's southern suburbs, three routes are realistic: an agent listing, a sale you manage yourself, or an as-is cash purchase. Owners live in about 70% of Henrietta homes and the rest are rented.

At a midpoint value of $223,700, even a few thousand dollars of commission or repairs cuts deeply into your proceeds. Price the work before you choose. A house needing only paint and a deep clean can go to market. One with a failing furnace, a wet basement or years of put-off upkeep may net about the same through a quick as-is sale.

  • Listing: the widest audience and usually the best price, at the cost of commission, repairs and a buyer's loan schedule.
  • By owner: you save the commission and take on pricing, showings and the contract.
  • As-is cash: fewer steps, and often a closing day of your choosing, at a price that covers the repairs.

Whatever you lean toward, get each offer in writing, showing the price, the date and each side's closing costs.

In southern Monroe County, Henrietta is roughly seven miles from downtown Rochester. The Genesee River forms its western edge, with Brighton to the north, Pittsford and Mendon to the east and Rush to the south. The town includes the hamlets of East Henrietta and West Henrietta and Riverton, a planned community. Rush-Henrietta Central School District serves it. Buyers like the quick Thruway and I-390 access, the 17.6 minute average commute, and the campus and retail district that keep the town busy.

About 48,800 people live here, 3.6% more than at the 2020 base. The 2025 estimate is 48,832 residents in 17,959 households of about 2.34 people. Owners occupy 69.8% of homes. The midpoint monthly cost for an owner with a mortgage is $1,720, rent is $1,344, and household income is $85,943. Just 78.7% of residents were at the same address a year earlier, which suggests turnover and plenty of renters. If your house was a rental, keep its rent history handy.

sections.h2: Property tax bills and where to pay
sections.html:
Henrietta's Receiver of Taxes is the Town Clerk's office. Two separate bills come from it each year.

Henrietta tax bills
BillMailedDue
Combined bill, Town and CountyLast business day of DecemberFebruary 10
SchoolLast business day of AugustOctober 1 in full, or a first installment by September 15

Town Hall takes school tax payments only until early November. After that, any balance goes to the Monroe County Treasurer, who sets a cutoff in November for school tax payments, and anything still owing after that rolls onto the following year's Combined bill. The Treasurer can give you the current cutoff. Confirm at closing that the school bill is paid in full, so nothing carries onto the next owner's bill.

  • Town Clerk tax office: mail to Receiver of Taxes, Henrietta, P.O. Box 579, Henrietta, NY 14467; duplicate bills at 585-359-7035.
  • Monroe County Treasurer: 39 West Main Street, Room B-2, Rochester, NY 14614; phone 585-753-1200.
  • Online: the Monroe County Real Property Portal displays bills and what has been paid.

Due dates are the same with escrow. When a lender pays your taxes, it gets the bill, and after the loan is paid off you file a Bank Code Removal Request Form so the bill comes to you again.

The Assessor's Office prepares the annual assessment roll, runs the grievance and tax certiorari process, administers exemptions including STAR, and manages the town's continuous revaluation. The town's assessor is a New York State certified assessor appointed to a six-year term. The office phone is 585-359-7032.

Ask it two things before you list. First, which exemptions the house carries, since STAR appears only on the school bill. Second, whether your parcel is part of any exemption correction. A notice on the office's page says some limited-income senior and disability exemption holders may get corrected school tax bills, and that an increase would be added to the 2027-28 school bill. A buyer will want to know what the taxes will be after the sale, so ask what applies to a new owner.

For a grievance, contact the office early in the year for the current window and form. Bring evidence of value to back it up, because the owner has to show the assessment is too high.

The state's transfer tax is $2 per $500 of price, and it falls on the seller unless the contract says otherwise. Form TP-584 reports the tax. Residences bought for $1 million or more carry an extra 1%, paid by the buyer.

For Henrietta deeds, the place is the Monroe County Clerk's downtown office, 39 W. Main Street, Room 101, Rochester, NY 14614, open 9 to 5 on weekdays. Email is the way to reach staff. The Clerk is the official registrar of deeds, mortgages, judgments and liens, and your attorney or title company normally brings the deed in.

Ask the Town Clerk's tax office for a duplicate bill before showings begin, and check that the school bill shows as paid. Ask which exemptions the Assessor has recorded. STAR appears only on the school bill, so a buyer will want to know what the bill will look like for a new owner. If a mortgage remains, request a payoff figure. Last, pick a closing date that fits your move, since a cash buyer can often work to it. Write that date into the offer, along with who pays each closing cost, so nothing is left to argue about at the table.

Figure out your take-home first, then the calendar. A listing can fetch more, but commission, repairs and the lender's timeline come with it. An as-is cash sale gives up part of the price in return for speed and certainty.

  • Agree on who pays the transfer tax and closing costs.
  • Put proof of funds and the closing date on paper.
  • Check the school and Combined Town and County tax status with the Town Clerk or the Monroe County portal.
  • With tenants in the house, ask how the buyer will treat the lease.

In both cases an attorney or title company searches title, prorates taxes and files the deed. Paying cash means no wait for a loan, but any lien or unpaid tax still has to be cleared before title passes.

faqs.q: When are Henrietta property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 10 is the due date for the Combined Town and County bill. The school bill is due October 1 in full, or in two parts with the first by September 15. Mailings go out on the last business day of December and of August.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Henrietta school tax balance late in the year?
faqs.a: With the Monroe County Treasurer, at 39 West Main Street, Room B-2 in Rochester, phone 585-753-1200. Town Hall stops taking school tax in early November, and the county sets its own November cutoff.

faqs.q: Who handles exemptions and assessment grievances in Henrietta?
faqs.a: Call the Town Assessor's Office at 585-359-7032. It prepares the roll, runs grievances and tax certiorari, and administers exemptions such as STAR.

faqs.q: Who pays the New York transfer tax on a Henrietta sale?
faqs.a: Normally the seller, at $2 per $500 of price, though a contract can move it to the buyer. A separate 1% tax applies on residential sales of $1 million or more, and the buyer pays it.

faqs.q: Where are deeds recorded for a house in Henrietta?
faqs.a: Monroe County's Clerk records them, at an office on West Main Street in downtown Rochester. That office keeps the county's official files on deeds, mortgages, judgments and liens.
